# MIDAS band base rates: silver / platinum / palladium (gold as reference)

**Read-only research pass, 2026-09-25.** Instrument: `band_stats.py` (same folder). Every table from §0 onward is generated by the script into `band_stats_body.md` and appended below verbatim. **This preamble (the summary, data notes and candidate list) is hand-written from those tables.** Data: yfinance, `auto_adjust=False` Close, no-roll ETFs SLV / PPLT / PALL / GLD (+ CPER used only for correlations). **Last complete close used: 2026-09-24.** The 2026-09-25 bar was dropped because the run was at 09:39 ET, so that bar was still an intraday partial. No bands are proposed here. The last section lists **candidates for the operator**, each with its historical fire rate.

## Headline figures (as of the 2026-09-24 close)

| metal | close | d200 today (rank full / 2020+) | r63 today (rank full / 2020+) | dd252 today (rank full / 2020+) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SLV | 57.62 | **−12.6%** (p10 / p7) | +10.0% (p74 / p70) | **−45.4%** (p2 / p2) |
| PPLT | 15.90 | **−10.1%** (p15 / p11) | +9.7% (p83 / p72) | **−37.0%** (p1 / p3) |
| PALL | 23.00 | **−14.9%** (p14 / p23) | +6.9% (p63 / p67) | **−38.1%** (p11 / p24) |
| GLD | 391.69 | −5.9% (p11 / p7) | +6.0% (p67 / p60) | −21.0% (p5 / p2) |

Windows run from the first valid metric day (SLV 2007, PPLT and PALL 2010–11, GLD 2005) and, separately, from 2020-01-02 (n = 1,691 days). The rank is the share of days in the window with a value at or below today's.

**What the numbers say, in plain terms:**
1. **A 200-day-average band would have missed the 2026 silver collapse for four months.** SLV's closing high was 105.60 on 2026-01-28. On 2026-01-30 it was 28.6% below that high while still **72% above** its 200-day average, because the average had been dragged up by the +144% run-up (the peak d200 reading, on 1/28). The copper-style grid applied to silver would have fired Yellow (−5%) only on **2026-06-10 @ 57.66**, 92 sessions after the high, with the ETF already −45.4%. Orange (−12%) would have fired on **06-24 @ 51.78** (−51.0%) and Red (−20%) on **07-16 @ 50.39** (−52.3%). A drawdown-from-252-day-high band fired within 2–3 sessions (−20% on **01-30 @ 75.44**, −30% on **02-02 @ 72.44**).
2. **The quarterly-return (r63) band is silent today.** Its 63-session base is the June low, so r63 is now positive on all four metals. That is the same blind spot the copper QoQ leg has.
3. **The 2026 crossings for PPLT and PALL follow the same pattern.** The d200 −5% band fired 92 sessions (PPLT) and 40 sessions (PALL) after the high, with the ETFs already −35.9% and −34.2%. dd252 −20% fired at 5 and 11 sessions. PPLT **never crossed d200 −20%** in 2026: its trough was −18.2% on 06-30. PALL crossed −20% on 06-24 @ 21.12, and that episode is still ONGOING (78 sessions below −12%).
4. **The three metals mostly move on one shared root.** Correlations of daily returns from 2020: SLV–GLD 0.79, SLV–PPLT 0.71, PPLT–PALL 0.64. Over the last 120 sessions they rose to 0.87 / 0.82 / 0.82, and even CPER–SLV was 0.76. The d200 −12% crossings in 2026 came within 15 sessions of each other (PALL 06-03, PPLT 06-23, SLV 06-24). Count that as one root, not three signals. Historically all three were below −12% together on only 6% of the days on which any one of them was.

## Data problems (read before citing)

- **Splits.** Yahoo back-adjusts the Close series for SLV's 10:1 split (2008-07-24), PPLT's 10:1 split (2026-05-18) and PALL's 5:1 split (2026-05-18). I checked the adjustment: the ETF/front-month-futures price ratio stays continuous across 2026-05-15 → 05-19 (PPLT 0.00897 → 0.00906, PALL 0.01800 → 0.01803), and no daily move above 15% falls on a split date. Price levels quoted before a split are split-adjusted, not the prints of the day. Ratio metrics are unaffected. Volumes are Yahoo's (also split-adjusted), so share counts from before and after a split are not comparable.
- **The real crash days are genuine and cross-checked against futures.** On 2026-01-30 SLV fell −28.5% (SI=F −31.3%), PPLT −18.4% (PL=F −19.0%) and PALL −15.7% (PA=F −15.6%). From the 2026 high to 09-24, SLV is −45.4% vs SI=F −44.9%, PPLT −37.0% vs PL=F −38.7%, and PALL −38.1% vs PA=F −41.5%. Futures were used only for this check and never for returns. The ETF high dates are 1/23–1/28, while the futures closing highs are on 1/26 (settlement timing).
- **Inception effects.** PPLT and PALL start 2010-01-08, so their full-window d200 starts 2010-10-22 and dd252 starts 2011-01-06. **The PGM full-window rates therefore exclude 2008, while SLV and GLD include it.** For like-for-like comparisons use the 2020+ rows. No PGM low-liquidity problem was found: first-year median volume was 620k (PPLT) and 905k (PALL) shares, with zero days of zero volume and no calendar gaps (max gap 5 calendar days = holiday weekend / 2012 Sandy closure; 0 missing days vs the union calendar). The ETF close vs NAV premium was not examined.
- **CPER is unreliable before about 2016.** It has 329 zero-volume days, a first-year median volume of 300 shares, and bad-print reversals (2014-12-04 −33% / 12-05 +50%; 2015-02-02 −29% / 02-03 +46%). It is used only in the 2020+ and 120-session correlations, which exclude those prints. The 2025-07-30 −19.3% move is real (the US copper-tariff exemption). CPER holds futures, so its returns carry roll yield but no roll jumps.
- **Expense-ratio drag** (about 0.4–0.6%/yr) lowers the ETF slightly relative to spot. It is negligible for d200 (about 0.3% over 200 sessions) and small for dd252.
- **Small samples.** 2020+ is 6.7 years. Episode counts there run from 0 to 17, so a rate like "0.15/yr" is **one episode**. Episode rates also depend on the reset rule (stated in §4 / §4b). A different reset changes the count.
- **The 2025–26 spike and crash make up a large share of 2020+ history.** SLV's +144% d200 peak and the crash that followed shape the 2020+ tails (for example, SLV 2020+ d200 p99 = +79.9%). Recent-window percentiles are therefore regime-heavy.

## What the data suggests: candidate thresholds for the operator (not proposals)

Fire rates are episodes per year, full window / 2020+ (§4b). "2026 catch" is the first firing after the 2026 high (§5).

| metal | candidate | fire rate full / 2020+ | 2026 catch (after the high) |
|---|---|---|---|
| SLV | d200 < −5 / −12 / −20% (copper grid) | 1.33 / 1.04 · 0.87 / 1.04 · 0.36 / 0.45 | s92 @ −45% · s101 @ −51% · s116 @ −52% |
| SLV | dd252 < −20 / −30 / −40% | 0.77 / 0.89 · 0.41 / 0.45 · 0.21 / 0.15 | s2 @ −29% · s3 @ −31% · s36 (03-20) @ −42% |
| SLV | d200 > +30 / +40% (spike) | 0.36 / 0.45 · 0.20 / 0.30 | +40% fired 2025-10-10 and stayed on through the 01-28 peak (+144%) |
| PPLT | d200 < −10 / −15 / −20% | 1.26 / 1.78 · 0.57 / 0.74 · 0.13 / 0.15 | −12% at s103 @ −41%; −20% not reached |
| PPLT | dd252 < −20 / −30% | 0.76 / 0.89 · 0.19 / 0.30 | s5 @ −23% · s39 @ −31% |
| PPLT | d200 > +30 / +40% | 0.13 / 0.30 · 0.06 / 0.15 | +40% fired 2025-06-26, peak +88% on 01-23 |
| PALL | d200 < −12 / −20 / −25% | 1.13 / 1.78 · 0.44 / 0.59 · 0.38 / 0.45 | s87 @ −36% · s101 @ −43% · not reached |
| PALL | dd252 < −20 / −30 / −40% | 0.51 / 0.74 · 0.51 / 0.59 · 0.38 / 0.59 | s11 @ −21% · s36 @ −31% · s90 (06-08) @ −41% |
| PALL | d200 > +30 / +40% | 0.31 / 0.45 · 0.25 / 0.30 | +40% fired 2025-10-08, peak +61.5% on 12-26 |
| GLD (ref) | d200 < −12% · dd252 < −20% | 0.14 / 0.00 · 0.34 / 0.30 | d200 −12% never reached · dd252 −20% at s88 |

Observations the operator may weigh (these are observations, not rules):
- **The copper grid (−5 / −12 / −20) fits silver's d200 distribution.** SLV's full-window p10 is −13.0 and p5 is −18.0. The grid does not fit **palladium**: PALL spent 28.9% of 2020+ days below −12% and 11.8% below −20%, and its 2020+ median dd252 is −27.8%. A −12% Orange on PALL would have been "on" for most of 2022–24. PALL needs wider lines, or lines relative to its own distribution. **Platinum's** d200 −20% is a very rare event: 2 episodes in 16 years (2015-11 and 2020-03).
- **A d200-only downside band is structurally late after a parabolic run-up.** In 2026 it fired only after 45–52% of SLV's fall. dd252 caught the collapse in days, but it fires often in trendless years (SLV dd252 < −20% on 33.9% of all days). A d200 spike band (> +40%) was already firing in October 2025, before the top. n is small (4 SLV episodes at +40% in 19.6 years), so this is not evidence of predictive power.
- **Shared root:** when silver, platinum and palladium bands fire in the same few weeks, count them as one dollar / real-rate / risk-off root (see §6). This matches the MIDAS independence rule.

Definitions: **d200** = close / SMA200 − 1; **r63** = 63-session return; **dd252** = close / rolling-252-session max − 1. Percentile rank = % of days in window with value ≤ today.
